trust_decision.summary: The self-hosted remote cache server and the cache artifacts it serves are untrusted: an artifact may only be extracted under <cache>/<hash>, and only the task's declared outputs, confined to the workspace root and without following destination symlinks, may be written back into the workspace; decided in the native cache layer (http_remote_cache.rs / cache.rs / file_ops.rs) at the HTTP cache boundary.

landing_point.why: The tar entry name from the server is joined onto the cache output dir and handed to Archive::unpack with no containment; that `output_dir.join(entry_path)` + `entry.unpack` pair is the textbook zip-slip sink and the first place a reader of the advisory summary looks.

fix_sites.entry_point: HttpRemoteCache.retrieve (HTTP GET {NX_SELF_HOSTED_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER}/v1/cache/:hash, reached from DbCache.get / getBatch)
fix_sites.module_kind: native remote-cache HTTP client (Rust napi, tar extraction)

fix_sites.entry_point: NxCache.copyFilesFromCache (napi) and NxCache.applyRemoteCacheResults (napi, via cache.rs:291), reached from DbCache.get and task-orchestrator.ts:523
fix_sites.module_kind: native cache store (Rust napi, cache->workspace restore)
native cache store (Rust napi, workspace->cache store)

fix_sites.entry_point: shared copy primitive: pub fn _copy used by put (cache.rs:256) and restore (cache.rs:407), plus the public napi copy() (file_ops.rs:16) used by the legacy TS cache
fix_sites.module_kind: low-level file-ops helper (Rust, no cache knowledge; looks out of scope)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver fixing "zip-slip in the self-hosted remote cache" can argue the generic copy helper in file_ops.rs (and the store direction in NxCache.put) is not part of the remote-cache path at all: no HTTP, no tar, it is just the local cache's file copier, so the traversal must be stopped where the artifact is extracted.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate symlinked outputs must still be restored as symlinks (pnpm/bun linker and Next.js standalone layouts): an over-broad fix that rejects or dereferences symlinks pointing outside the workspace breaks cache restore for those builds.

O6_input_shapes: relative output that climbs out with `..` (e.g. `../../escape`)
absolute output inside the workspace (relativized, must NOT be rejected)
mixed list where one entry escapes and another is valid (whole put/restore must fail)
tar entry name that is an absolute path
tar symlink entry followed by an entry writing through it
tar hardlink entry whose target is outside the output dir
pre-existing symlink at the destination inside the workspace (restore must not write through it, must still delete safely)
artifact containing files beyond the declared outputs (must not be restored)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second copy primitive (e.g. copy_dir_all_excluding / a copy_within variant) used by only one of the two directions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already has two near-duplicate directory walkers (the top-level _copy branch and copy_dir_all's recursion); a maintainer adding a confined variant for restore would plausibly add a third rather than thread a boundary through both.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a normalizing wrapper around _expand_outputs applied only on the restore path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Outputs are expanded twice (put at cache.rs:246, restore at cache.rs:392); a maintainer fixing restore-only would naturally add the check inside the expander or at one call site, leaving the store direction open.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second artifact reader on the store/PUT side (e.g. round-tripping the tarball through the server)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already owns both directions; a feature such as verification or re-upload would add another path that consumes server-supplied entry names.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal / zip-slip (archive entry and declared-output paths escaping their base) with CWE-59 symlink following on restore

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace `output_dir.join(entry_path)` + `entry.unpack(...)` in download_and_extract_from_result with `entry.unpack_in(&output_dir)` (or reject `..`/absolute entry names) and stop, leaving the whole-cache-dir copy into the workspace, the symlinked-parent write-through, and the `{workspaceRoot}/../..` output declarations untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Remote-cache plugins resolved by DbCache.getRemoteCache (s3/gcs/azure/shared-fs, external packages) can hand back an arbitrary CachedResult.outputsPath; those packages are outside this repository and were not examined.
